app.tagline: Encrypted mail for humans and agents

setup.title: Welcome to your inbox
setup.subtitle: Pigeon Mail talks to your own server. Paste an API key and the mailbox opens — no password, no third-party relay.
setup.label: API key
setup.hint: Keys are created in the dashboard under Account → API keys. A key with the full scope unlocks reading, sending and settings.
setup.invalid: That doesn’t look like a Pigeon API key. It should start with pk_.
setup.securityTitle: Your key never leaves this browser
setup.securityBody: It is stored in this device’s local storage and sent only to your own server as a Bearer token.
setup.step1Body: Inbound mail arrives sealed, with SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts attached.
setup.step2Body: Open a message to decrypt it locally — bodies are never stored in the clear.
setup.step3Body: Reply, forward or compose; delivery is queued and retried automatically.

mail.emptyInboxBody: New mail will land here, already decrypted for you and verified by SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
mail.emptySentBody: Compose your first message — Pigeon queues it, retries it and tells you when it lands.
mail.emptySearchBody: Try a different sender or subject.
mail.selectBody: Choose a conversation on the left to read it here, with its authentication verdicts and attachments.
mail.errorTitle: The mailbox is out of reach
mail.errorBody: We couldn’t reach the Pigeon API. Check that the server is running and that the key still has access.
mail.forbiddenBody: The key is valid but lacks the read or full scope. Create a stronger key in the dashboard and sign in again.
mail.demoBanner: Demo preview — the server is unreachable, so sample mail is shown.
mail.htmlOnly: This message only had an HTML part; the text below was extracted for safe reading.
mail.sealedBody: This message is still sealed. A key with the full scope can decrypt it.
mail.noBody: This message has no readable body.
mail.sentNote: Sent messages keep metadata and delivery status only — the sealed body stays on the server.
mail.emptySpamBody: Messages reported as spam will appear here.
mail.emptyTrashBody: Deleted messages stay here until you empty the trash.

drafts.title: Drafts
drafts.empty: No drafts yet. Anything you save from the compose box shows up here.

compose.title: New message
compose.subject: Subject
compose.sendError: The send failed. Check the recipients and try again.
compose.requiredTo: At least one recipient is required.
compose.invalidEmail: One of the addresses isn’t valid.
compose.tooManyFiles: You can attach up to 10 files.
compose.tooLarge: Attachments can’t exceed 25 MB in total.
compose.attachFailed: One of the files couldn’t be read.
compose.scheduleFuture: Pick a time in the future.
compose.confirmReplace: Replace what you wrote with this template?

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Keys, webhooks and how the mailbox feels.
settings.keysBody: Keys authenticate the API, the MCP server and this webmail. Secrets are shown once.
settings.keysEmpty: No keys yet. Create one to connect a client.
settings.keyCreated: Copy this key now — it won’t be shown again.
settings.webhooksBody: Pigeon POSTs signed events to your endpoint as mail moves through the queue.
settings.webhooksEmpty: No webhooks yet. Point one at your app to receive delivery events.
settings.webhookCreated: Copy the signing secret now — it won’t be shown again.
settings.preferencesBody: Language, theme and motion are stored on this device.
settings.languageHelp: Interface language. Dates and times follow it too.
settings.themeHelp: Light for daylight, dark for late-night triage.
settings.motionHelp: Turn every animation off, or respect your system setting.
settings.dangerBody: Signing out forgets the API key stored in this browser.
settings.forbidden: This key is missing the full scope, so keys and webhooks can’t be managed here.
settings.loadError: We couldn’t load this section. Check the server and try again.
settings.templatesBody: Reusable message bodies. Every template shows up in the compose box, ready to fill in.
settings.noTemplates: No templates yet. Create one below and it appears in the compose picker.
settings.tplBodyPlaceholder: Hi Ana, here is what you asked for…
settings.testNeedsTo: Enter at least one address to send the test to.
settings.tplDuplicate: A template with that name already exists.
settings.domainsBody: Domains this account may send from, with the DNS records they need.
settings.noDomains: No domains yet. Add one in the dashboard to send from your own address.
settings.dnsHint: Publish these records with your DNS provider. Verification runs again on the next check.
settings.suppressionsBody: Addresses Pigeon never sends to: manual blocks, hard bounces and complaints.
settings.noSuppressions: Nothing suppressed — every address is deliverable.

auth.unauthorized: This key was rejected. Sign in with a valid key.

admin.title: Admin console
admin.subtitle: People, roles and where the mail for your domains goes.
admin.volumeAria: Bar chart of sends per day over the last 14 days
admin.noOrgBody: An organization groups the mailboxes of a team. Every member keeps their own address and their own sealed mail — joining a team never merges inboxes. You become its owner.
admin.inviteTokenOnce: Copy this invitation token now — it won't be shown again. They use it as the login code.
admin.bootstrapTokenOnce: Copy this bootstrap token now — it won't be shown again. They use it as the login code.
admin.lastOwner: The last owner can't be demoted — promote somebody else first.
admin.catchallBody: Where mail for an unknown address of a domain lands. Without a rule the server answers 550.
admin.privacyNote: Admins see accounts, roles and delivery metadata. Message bodies stay sealed: the admin cannot read user mail without the user's keys.
admin.notAdmin: You are not an organization admin
admin.notAdminBody: Only owners and admins see members, invitations and catch-all rules. With your role everything here stays read-only.
admin.catchallNoTarget: No member of this domain yet. Create the mailbox first, then route to it.

login.title: Sign in to Pigeon Mail
login.hint: Enter your account email. Two-factor verification is requested when enrolled.
login.error: Sign-in failed. Check the address and try again.

security.title: Two-factor authentication
security.body: TOTP second factor (RFC 6238) for this dashboard session. Works with Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password.
security.notEnrolled: Two-factor authentication is not enrolled yet. It protects every dashboard sign-in with a 6-digit code.
security.stepScan: Scan the secret (or copy the otpauth URI) with your authenticator app.
security.stepConfirm: Enter the 6-digit code from the app to activate.
security.recoveryOnce: Recovery codes — shown once. Store them somewhere safe; each works a single time.
